ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Energy Storage Devices

Capacitor
  A two- terminal electrical component that has the ability to store energy  in the form of electrical charge
  Has two conducting plates separated by a dielectric
  When a DC voltage is connected across the capacitor, one plate becomes  positive and the other negative 
  The charge accumulation on the plates causes a voltage or potential
   difference across the capacitor

Source:https://www.electronics-tutorials.ws/capacitor/cap_1.html

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Energy Storage Devices

Capacitance is the charge accumulation capability of a capacitor
  Charge (Q) stored in a capacitor is directly proportional to the voltage
    (V) developed across the capacitor; 
  Q = C × V, where C is the capacitance measured in farads
  Capacitance is directly proportional to area of plates (A) and inversely
    proportional to the distance between the two plates (D);

Source:https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Capacitor_types

Energy Storage Devices

Supercapacitors
   Also known as ultra capacitors or electrochemical double-layer capacitors(EDLC) 
   Are  energy storage devices that have high capacitance and are used to
    store large amounts of electrical charge
  Charge and discharge very quickly
  Capacitance is several thousand times that of a Capacitor 
  Capacitor -----     µF
  Supercapacitor -----    thousands of Farads

Construction:
	Electrodes: made of high surface area materials such as porous carbon, graphene, carbon  nanotubes and certain conducting polymers or carbon aerogel
      Electrolyte: KOH, H2SO4, Na2SO4
      Separator: an ion permeable separator is placed between the electrodes in order prevent electrical contact, but still allows ions from electrolyte to pass through e.g., porous polypropylene
